title: From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay, from the Minimum Wage to the Qantas CEO Salary
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary, including tax, super, and Medicare levy. Compare with the Qantas CEO salary and national minimum wage.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay equals hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week times 52 weeks, before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your usual weekly hours, then by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives $52,254.80 per year. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. Remember that casual loading (25%) is added on top of the base rate, not included in the rate you enter.

faqs.q: Does the Qantas CEO salary include super and bonuses?
faqs.a: The Qantas CEO's fixed annual remuneration (FAR) of $1.6 million is the base salary, excluding super and incentives. Super guarantee is paid on top (capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830). Short-term and long-term incentive plans can add up to 160% of FAR each, but are subject to performance conditions. For example, former CEO Alan Joyce had his FY23 remuneration reduced by $9.26 million due to performance issues.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. Modern awards set higher minimum rates for specific industries and occupations, plus penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database contains detailed rates. Always check your award if you have one, as it may pay more than the minimum wage.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay

If you're paid by the hour, you might wonder what that means over a full year. Whether you're comparing job offers, budgeting, or just curious, converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward. The basic formula is: **annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, that's hourly × 38 × 52. This article explains the calculation, how tax and super affect your take-home pay, and how even the highest salaries—like the Qantas CEO salary—are built on the same arithmetic.

### The Basic Conversion

Assume a 38-hour week (the standard full-time hours under many awards and the National Minimum Wage). For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Multiply by 38 gives $1,004.90 per week, and by 52 gives $52,254.80 per year. If you're a casual employee, you typically receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. That yields $1,255.90 per week and $65,306.80 annually. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page can help you run the numbers for your own rate.

But what if you work more or fewer hours? The formula adapts. A part-timer working 20 hours a week at $30/hour earns $600 per week, $31,200 annually. Always use your actual weekly hours. The fortnightly amount is simply weekly pay times two—useful for budgeting if you're paid fortnightly. For a 38-hour week at $26.44, that's $2,009.80 per fortnight before tax.

### Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross figure, you need to estimate tax. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (generally). For a single person earning $52,255 (minimum wage full-time), the tax is roughly: nil on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 = $4,020, plus 30% on $7,255 = $2,176.50, total $6,196.50. Medicare adds $1,045.10. Take-home is about $45,013.40. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide has more detail.

For higher earners, the marginal rates bite. Consider the Qantas CEO salary: Vanessa Hudson's fixed annual remuneration (FAR) is $1.6 million per year, as disclosed in her employment agreement. That's not an hourly rate—it's a fixed annual amount. But if we were to express it as an hourly equivalent for a 38-hour week, it would be $1,600,000 / (38 × 52) ≈ $809.72 per hour. That's over 30 times the minimum wage. However, the CEO's total package includes short-term and long-term incentives. For example, the target STIP is 100% of FAR, and the LTIP maximum is 160% of FAR. The Board also reduced former CEO Alan Joyce's FY23 remuneration by $9.26 million due to performance issues. This shows that even at the top, annual pay is subject to adjustments.

### Superannuation

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For the minimum wage earner, that's an extra $6,270.58 per year (12% of $52,254.80), but only up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For the Qantas CEO, 12% of $1.6 million would be $192,000, but the maximum base caps the super at $32,499.60 (12% of $270,830). So the CEO's super is limited, while lower earners get the full 12% on all earnings. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

### Award Rates and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage is the floor, but many employees are covered by modern awards that set higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Commission maintains the Modern Awards Pay Database with detailed rates. For example, a retail employee might have a higher base rate plus penalties for weekends. Casual loading of 25% is common, but it's added on top of the base rate—never include it in the rate you type into a calculator. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) article explains.

### Comparing with Average Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 annually. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week ($82,118.40 annually). The Qantas CEO salary of $1.6 million is about 15 times the full-time average. But remember, the CEO's role carries immense responsibility and is subject to performance conditions.

### Putting It All Together

To estimate your annual pay:

1. Determine your hourly base rate (excluding casual loading).
2. Multiply by your usual weekly hours (if full-time, use 38).
3. Multiply by 52 to get annual gross.
4. Subtract estimated tax and Medicare levy using the 2026–27 rates.
5. Add super (12% of ordinary earnings, capped) as a separate benefit.

Our [reference tables](/data) provide quick lookups for common rates. And if you're comparing job offers, remember that salary packaging, allowances, and penalty rates can change the picture. The formula is a starting point.

The Qantas CEO salary example shows that even at the highest levels, the basic arithmetic of hours and weeks applies—though the numbers are vastly different. Whether you earn $26.44 per hour or $809 per hour, understanding your annual pay helps you plan for tax, super, and your financial future.
